text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- National Assembly Chairman Nong Duc Manh has praised Russia's help in developing the gas and oil industry.
-- More than 105,000 boatpeople have been repatriated from refugee camps across Southeast Asia over the past five years.
-- The European Commission will launch an economic and financing programme to provide improved financial services to small and medium enterprises in Vietnam.
-- A scientist with Vietnam's Institute of Atomic Energy says plutonium left in the country following a failed U.S. retrieval operation in 1975 is being kept under proper safeguards.
-- The Asia Commercial Joint Stock Bank has become the third bank in Vietnam authorized to accept foreign shareholders.
-- The Government has called for an urgent nationwide programme to combat increasing crime.
-- Deputy Prime Minister Nguyen Khanh has told journalists their reporting should follow Party and the State policies.
-- Vietnam has reiterated its determination to stop timber imports from Cambodia.
-- Vietnam held a celebration to mark the 47th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relation between Vietnam and China in Hanoi on Thursday.
-- The Ho Chi Minh City People's Committee says speeding up the equitization of state enterprises is a priority task for 1997.
